exact_claim: The strong-SYZ reference route must construct, for the prescribed nef isotropic class, an actual marked degeneration and a full smooth flat-cylinder limit in the original logarithmic coordinates, obtain an embedded special Lagrangian torus in the angular coordinate isotopy class, rotate it to a nonprojective holomorphic Lagrangian torus supplying a semiample seed in that same class, and return by conditional semiampleness propagation. The full route is outside the old local clearing certificate.
hypotheses: Main theorem: X is a compact IHS Kahler manifold of dimension 2n, n>=1, and L is holomorphic with c1(L) nonzero, nef and BBF-isotropic.
The primitive integral class e and its positive sign are fixed in the full H2 lattice and marked deformation component; e need not remain of type (1,1) before rotation.

The prescribed-cusp family has smooth total space, reduced SNC central fiber, projective IHS smooth fibers, an extending polarization ample on smooth fibers, and the exact period/monodromy formulas with the original labelled e.
Torus theorem: complex dimension d>=2; trivial canonical smooth connected projective fibers; logarithmically extending nowhere-zero volume forms with I_t comparable to s^d, s=-log|t|.
Torus theorem: d+1 central components meet at one point with t=z0...zd and nonzero logarithmic volume coefficient at that point.
The metric is the polarized Ricci-flat metric scaled by s; the required limits and perturbations use actual logarithmic/angle coordinates, not arbitrary convergence charts.
Rotation criterion: T is compact connected oriented embedded special Lagrangian for I and i^*[omega_K]=0 in H2(T,R); the complex-torus conclusion additionally uses T diffeomorphic to a real 2n-torus.
The nonprojective torus input requires a holomorphic Lagrangian complex torus; the propagation input requires a semiample point in the same positive fixed-class component.
The b2>=5 restriction is on the separate finiteness corollary, not the main semiampleness theorem or the supplied-isotropic-class construction.
